text:
Maya: Hey team — acme-inc reports p95 ~850ms calling /v1/generate from us-east. They attached a trace that shows an unexpected hop to eu-west before returning. Request-ID: 01FZ9ABCD

Priya: can you drop the trace here and the client headers? especially any X-Region or X-Forwarded-For

Maya: paste from customer (anonymized):
```
traceroute to api.redwood.dev (35.195.11.23), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.0.1  0.6 ms  0.5 ms  0.5 ms
 2  100.64.0.1  2.1 ms  2.0 ms  2.0 ms
 3  203.0.113.5  12.4 ms  12.6 ms  12.5 ms
 4  35.195.11.23 (35.195.11.23)  420.1 ms  419.8 ms  421.0 ms
 5  34.117.12.2 (34.117.12.2)  422.4 ms  421.9 ms  422.2 ms
```

Santiago: hm that 35.195.x.x looked like a GCP egress IP, but the latency bumps align with an EU detour. Do we have any routing policy that could push egress to eu-west for that customer prefix? :eyes:

Maya: customer sent headers:
"X-Region: us-east-1"
"User-Agent: acme-internal/2.1"

Liam: FYI DeployBot shows a canary deployed yesterday 2024-03-21 03:21 that toggled "enable-regional-egress" flag for alpha targets. Could be related.

DeployBot: Canary c-20240321 completed - changes: routing.alpha.enableRegionalEgress = true

Priya: action plan: 1) Santiago - run traceroute+BGP dump from node that saw the detour 2) Check routing service egress-policy and recent canary diffs 3) If BGP leak/more-specific, coordinate with peering partner to withdraw or fix community tagging 4) Hold/rollback canary if it looks like the cause

Santiago: running now. quick excerpt of bgp table from affected edge node:
```
> show ip bgp 35.195.0.0/16
  35.195.11.0/24 via 198.51.100.10 (peer-xyz) [i] origin incomplete
    Nexthop 198.51.100.10 from AS65530, localpref 100, community [ 65530:200 ]
```

Santiago: looks like partner propagated a more-specific -> their AS is advertising the /24 towards eu-west. pushing an emergency BGP update to withdraw that prefix and re-assert our aggregate with local-prep. also reverting the alpha egress flag on the canary while we validate.

Maya: after the bgp withdraw + canary revert customer reports p95 down to ~120ms. they say the request-id 01FZ9ABCD now shows regional hop direct to us-east. :white_check_mark:

Liam: filing follow-up ticket INF-4321 to tighten canary rollout gating for routing-affecting flags and add monitoring for unexpected AS paths.

Priya: nice. please keep monitoring for 1h then close the thread. great triage and quick root-cause ID everyone. :thumbsup:
